b2786426-1415-41de-a476-386cdf9433ae.text_lemmatized: During interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.

bc544bca-afbe-45de-8b8a-02e7014d224e.data: In prophase, the chromosomes condense into X-shaped structures that can be easily seen under a microscope.

fa92056c-7067-4291-8033-5a4c591cebc0.data: During metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center (equator) of the cell.
fa92056c-7067-4291-8033-5a4c591cebc0.text_lemmatized: During metaphase, the chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center (equator) of the cell.

7360ce13-d375-407f-a8ce-91f8e2f37412.data: In anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, which pulls one chromatid to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.

76803003-0447-41be-a437-00cd1285ab3f.text_lemmatized: During telophase, a full set of chromosomes gather together at each pole of the cell, and a membrane forms around each set of chromosomes to create two new nuclei.
